To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of a lameness detection system can be improved by using individualised healthy reference data for each cow.

a lameness detection algorithm based on back postures derived from a camera has a high performance and that the historical window length is an important parameter in order to ensure that the historical data is meaningful for individual cows.

the use of individual thresholds for deviation detection in lameness detection systems can increase the accuracy of the system and the historical window length is an important parameter for individual threshold calculation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a tool to monitor lameness on a herd scale, which is based on a camera, and individualises the algorithm based on animal level data.
the optimisation of a lameness detection system based on camera derived back posture values for individual dairy cows.

developing an automated lameness detection system for dairy cattle that will be able to detect lameness in all cows on a farm, despite the fact that each cow will have its own individual response to the lameness problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
individualising lameness detection based on animal level healthy reference data improves the accuracy of deviation detection.
a system that is able to detect lameness in dairy cows with a sensitivity of 80% and a specificity of 80% is possible with a reference window length of 200 days.
a camera based system can accurately identify cows with lameness based on individualised deviation detection from an individual healthy reference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a lameness detection algorithm can be optimised for individual animals by tuning deviation thresholds based on individual historical data.
a camera based system for automated lameness detection can be tuned based on individual animal level historical data to achieve high performance on farm scale.
a camera based lameness monitoring system can be optimised by using individual healthy references based on historical data to ensure accurate monitoring of all animals on the farm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the historical reference window length should be carefully considered when designing lameness detection algorithms for use in large herds with high levels of animal turnover.
a lameness detection system should be individualised based on animal level data to maximise algorithm performance.
individualisation of lameness detection algorithms based on historical data is a viable approach to improve the accuracy of automated lameness detection systems.
